_note: Klingon interface. Written in English, unlike the Hungarian and Greek notes and like the Indonesian one, and for a reason rather than out of laziness: this note is documentation for whoever reviews the catalogue, and two thousand words of Klingon prose would be a far larger act of composition than the 318 strings it describes. SOURCE: every string is built from headwords in the published Klingon lexicon (TKD, its addendum, KGT, Talk Now! Klingon, and the qep'a' and qepHom'a' new-word releases) with the morphology TKD sections 3 and 4 documents. **No root here is an invention**, which is the same rule the corpus follows, and it is checkable the same way: strip a pronominal prefix and any suffixes and the remainder is a dictionary entry. REGISTER: the imperative, everywhere an English interface would use a bare verb. `yIpol` "save it", `yIngeH` "send it", `yIwIv` "choose it". Klingon has no T-V distinction and no politeness register in the European sense, so an imperative on a button is not brusque -- it is the only thing the grammar offers, and KGT's own examples of everyday instruction are imperatives (`Soj yIDIl!`, `DaH yIDIl!`). The prefix is `yI-` where the object is a thing and `HI-` where it is the reader (`HIboQ` "assist me", which is the studio's *Help me decide*), and `tI-` for a plural object (`Dochmey tIchel`). TERMS: `nav` is a sheet of paper and `tenwal` a page or printed face -- Klingon already keeps those apart, so no word had to be stretched. `war` is a column in a table and `wev` a row, both from the lexicon's own spreadsheet vocabulary, which is exactly the distinction `format.columnsPerFace` and `format.columnsShown` need and which English collapses into one word. Also: `'echletHom` = card, `ngutlh` = letter or glyph, `ngutlh Segh` = typeface, `ngutlh 'ab` = type size, `qalmuS` = colour, `rItlh` = ink, `veH` = margin (literally boundary), `rulvaH` = gap, `chevwI'` = divider, `yamtaw` = the printed rule, `botlh` = middle, `'utlh` = the header band, `potlh` = importance, `'ay'` = section, `De'` = data or content, `lol` = attitude or arrangement, used for the format panel. `'uj` renders the inch: it is a Klingon unit of 34.83 cm and not an inch at all, so the number beside it is right and the unit is a borrowing -- flagged here because it is the one term in the catalogue that is knowingly imprecise. Serif and Sans stay Latin, as they do in the Greek and Indonesian catalogues, and the romanisation-system names stay as printed, being standards initialisms. INTERPOLATION -- and Klingon comes out of this better than any other language here, for a reason worth stating. A placeholder is a plain string substitution, so the danger everywhere else is a template that needs its insert to inflect. **Klingon's noun suffixes have no allomorphs**: there is one locative `-Daq`, one ablative `-vo'`, one benefactive `-vaD`, and they attach to any noun unchanged. So `{language}Daq` is safe in a way `{language}ban/-ben` is not in Hungarian and `el {language}` is not in Spanish, and Klingon has no articles at all, so the article trap cannot arise either. Two traps do arise and both are avoided here. (1) **The type-4 possessives and the type-2 plurals are chosen by the noun's class, not by its sound**: `-wI'`/`-wIj` for "my" and `-pu'`/`-Du'`/`-mey` for the plural split on whether the noun is capable of using language, or is a body part, or is neither. That is a property of the *inserted* word, which a substitution cannot see, so no template in this file puts a possessive or a plural suffix after a placeholder. Where the English says "{language} pocket guide" the Klingon says `{language} 'echletHom`, two bare nouns in a noun-noun compound, which needs no suffix at all. (2) **Capitalisation is phonemic**: `q` and `Q` are different consonants and `I` is a vowel while `i` is not a letter. So no template may uppercase or lowercase a placeholder, and none does. This is also why the respelling table for a Klingon reader cannot use the `caps` stress device -- see data/respell/rules/tlh__tlh-TA.json. WORD ORDER: Klingon is object-verb-subject and puts a time element first, so a template with a placeholder in the middle of a clause has to be written so the insert is a whole noun phrase in its own slot. `{target} → {source}` and `{language} Hol` are the two shapes used; nothing here asks a placeholder to sit inside a verb. WHAT IS NOT HERE: `format.reserve.ios` and `.android` are `'ayvon` and `'anDroy'`, which are transliterations of brand names rather than lexicon entries, and are the only two coinages in the catalogue. They are marked here rather than left to be discovered. Klingon has no attested word for a tax refund, so `quiz.interest.business.hint` carries the English `tax`. FINISHING, AND THREE STRINGS THIS FILE DOES NOT HAVE. The sheet-finishing control arrived after the rest of the catalogue and only seven of its ten strings could be written. `format.finish.fold`, `cut.hint.fold` and `studio.foldOrder` are absent because **there is no verb for `fold` in the published Klingon lexicon** -- TKD and KGT give `pe'` cut and `SIj` slit and nothing for creasing paper -- and the rule this file runs on is that no root here is an invention. The two hint strings would additionally need `panel` and `crease`, which are not there either. So those three fall back to English, which the overlay design does per string, and `npm run i18n` reports it: 319 of 322 rather than a coined verb on a button nobody can look up. `format.finish` itself is `nav Segh`, "kind of sheet" -- English names the operation and Klingon names the result, the same move `ngutlh Segh` makes for Typeface, and the second knowingly loose term here after `'uj`. `roman.okrand` and `roman.appendix-e` stay as printed: every one of the eleven `roman.*` keys already does, `Hepburn` and `McCune-Reischauer` included, so transcribing Okrand's name while leaving Hepburn's alone would make one menu disagree with itself. Whether pIqaD changes that was the question, and the answer is that the menu labels a column of *Latin* letters and this catalogue is romanised Klingon throughout -- the interface is the app's chrome, not the card.

_ornament_note: Style labels use descriptive editorial paraphrases: mIllogh Segh (picture type), porDu' mIllogh (leaf picture), tlheghmey mIllogh (rope picture), Hov QuQ (star engine). These are not canonical names for the designs. yu'egh (wave), tlhegh (rope), Hov (star) and QuQ (engine) are TKD vocabulary; see https://klingonska.org/dict/. The low-ink hint says ordinary rules are used with little ink, and the chosen picture type returns when little ink is no longer used.
_board_note: Conversation-board and beacon strings. Every root is TKD or its addendum, as in the rest of this file: jang (answer, reply), SoQ (be closed), laj (accept), mI' (number), ghItlh (write), mev (stop, cease), Hot (touch, feel), poH (period of time), tup (minute), rep (hour), jaj (day), ghap (or, joining nouns) and 'ar (how many, how much -- TKD 6.4) are TKD; naQ (be full, be whole, be entire) and latlh (additional one, other one) are TKDA. beacon.help is ghoQaH, the canon form data/lang/tlh/emergency.csv already carries for emergency-medical.help (src=Star Trek VI): its object is plural, so it says "help us" rather than "help", and it stays romanised because that row carries no pIqaD either. TWO STRINGS ARE REWORDED rather than translated, because the English is not sayable. board.amount is poH 'ar, "how much time": 'ar follows the noun it counts, so a bare "how many" is not a Klingon phrase, and the corpus already composes it this way at time-scheduling.how-long-does-it-take. beacon.dismiss is mevmeH yIHot, "touch it so that it stops", which drops "anywhere" -- jIH is the viewing screen, but it is also the pronoun "me", so jIH yIHot would read as "touch me". WHAT IS NOT HERE: beacon.sos. SOS is a Morse sequence rather than an abbreviation of words, and every roman.* key in this file already leaves a standards initialism as printed, so the Latin letters fall back from English unchanged. SECOND PASS -- the clock and the bare number, all six added. board.atTime is rep, TKD's noun for an hour, which is how canon states a time of day (wa'vatlh rep is 01:00); the duration tile beside it keeps poH, TKD's noun for a period of time, so the two tiles carry the clock/duration contrast on Okrand's own pair of words and nothing is compounded. board.time is nuq rep "what hour?", the form data/lang/tlh/time.csv already carries at time-scheduling.what-time-is-it. board.number and board.otherNumber are the bare mI'. board.notATime is rep yIwIv "choose the hour": wIv (choose, select) is TKD, and the object-then-imperative shape is the one mI' naQ yIghItlh already uses. board.notANumber repeats board.notAnAmount word for word, because the two English strings are the same string. RESIDUAL RISK, recorded rather than hidden: hours of duration are also counted in rep (cha' rep, two hours), so rep... is unambiguous only because latlh poH... stands beside it. THIRD PASS -- the board's own chrome and the eight topic names, fifty-two of the fifty-four. Roots new to this note, every one from the published lexicon: chegh (return, TKD), ghu' (situation, TKD), Hoch (all, TKD), QIn (message, KGT), tetlh (roll, scroll, list, KGT), ghum (sound an alarm, TKD), buS (concentrate on, focus on, TKD), chIl (lose, TKDA), Seng (trouble, noun, TKD), rop (disease, noun, TKD), 'oy' (ache, pain, noun, TKD), qaS (occur, happen, TKD), ghaj (have, TKD), ngaS (contain, TKD), Sop (eat, TKD), je' (buy, TKD), leng (travel, TKD), ghom (meet, TKD), ghorgh (when?, TKD), nuv (person, TKD), Soj (food, TKDA), He (course, route, TKD), poH (period of time, TKD), chach (emergency, TKD), tlhe' (turn, TKD), ruch (proceed, TKDA), leS (rest, relax, TKD), maj (good, exclamation, TKD 5.5), pagh (or, between sentences, TKD 5.3, and the numeral zero, TKD), volchaH (shoulder, TKD), mong (neck, TKD), porgh (body, TKD), 'ay' (section, part, TKD), and lupwI' (bus, CK and KGT), ra'wI' (commander, TKD) and yaH (duty station, TKD) in the compounds data/lang/tlh/travel.csv already uses for a taxi and a platform. THE EIGHT TOPIC NAMES say what this catalogue and data/registry/section-titles/tlh.csv already say rather than coining beside them: chach is colour.alert and the emergency-medical section title; He, poH and Soj are the directions, time-scheduling and food-ordering section titles; nuvpu' yIghom is quiz.interest.social word for word and lengmeH is colour.move word for word; je'meH takes the -meH label shape from the shopping section title je'meH mu'mey, the same shape jatlhmeH and lengmeH already use. Soj names the food and not the act of dining out, and lengmeH the purpose and not the getting-around, because Klingon has no noun for either -- recorded here rather than compounded into existence. FIVE STRINGS ARE REWORDED. board.someMissing drops "on this board": {count} mu'tlhegh mughlu'pu'be', and mughlu'pu'be' is gallery.notTranslated unchanged; a number precedes an unsuffixed noun (TKD 5.2), so the placeholder cannot force a plural. board.noBoards is pagh ghu' tu'lu', "there are no situations" -- pagh is TKD's zero, tu'lu' the existential food-ordering.is-a-table-available already uses, and ghu' is what board.pickTopic and board.allTopics call a board, because there is no noun for a panel of buttons. board.turn drops "sideways": mu'mey yItlhe'moH, "make the words turn"; jIr (rotate) is KGT but the control is a toggle and not a direction, so tlhe' with the causative -moH (TKD 4.2.2) is used. boards.emergency.attention is yIghum, "sound the alarm", there being no verb for attracting attention. boards.emergency.lostTitle is Seng, "trouble", above the narrower tile vIchIlpu' "I have lost it": the English pairs a narrow button with a broad heading, and this keeps that relation without a noun for theft. board.wrongPair is object-verb-subject with both placeholders in bare noun-phrase slots and no suffix on either, as the rule at the top of this note requires: {language} Hol mu'tlheghmey ghajbe' {board}. board.docTitle is ja'chuqmeH (ja'chuq, discuss, confer, TKD) because there is no noun for a conversation, and it takes the same -meH label shape. board.menu is tetlh, a list: HIDjolev is TKD's own gloss for "menu" but it is a bill of fare, and the control opens a list of settings. THE ONE SPLIT THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE is boards.spa.focusOn over boards.body.*. Klingon puts the object before the verb, so a heading above its own objects has them in the wrong order; the heading is instead the complete clause porgh 'ay' yIbuS, "focus on a body part", and the four buttons are possessed nouns under it -- volchaHDu'wIj, DubwIj, mongwIj, qamDu'wIj, with -Du' for body parts and -wIj for a possessor of a thing (TKD 3.3.2, 3.3.4). WHAT IS NOT HERE. boards.spa.title: there is no word for massage anywhere in the published lexicon, and data/lang/tlh carries no massage-spa rows at all, so the board's name falls back to English whole. boards.emergency.sos: the English is "Flash SOS" and there is no verb for flashing -- boch is to shine and wov is to be bright, and neither takes the Latin letters as an object -- so it falls back for the same reason beacon.sos does.
